In 1977, CBF-FM-8 96.5 was established, it is a Class C channel of Ici Radio-Canada Premiere based at Trois-Rivieres working in Mauricie area. In 1976, the Francophone radio was licensed as a CBF-AM Montreal’s rebroadcast transmitter. It would telecast on ERP of 4326 w and 100.1 MHz respectively. In 1977, the transmitter hit the waves for the first time. In 1985, the frequency was flipped to 88.1 Mhz. The station was separated from Montreal AM station by the struggle of Canadian Broadcasting Corporation, and therefore a new license was granted by Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunication Commission to start an independent full-time channel known to be CBF-FM-8 telecasting in Trois-Rivieres. The proposed local transmission at the beginning was 5 hours per week which would contain content and news focusing on Cultural, regional, social, economic and political issues. On 22 July 2003, CRTC allowed some transformation in authorized contours, according to which the ERP would be increased up to 66700 w with the frequency of 96.5 MHz. Currently Ici Radio-Canada Premiere channel with 4 FM in different regions of Quebec. The *Trois-Rivieres *station airs Samedi et rien d’autre and Facteur matinal, which are among the famous shows of the radio. On 28 May 2013, the license for CBF-FM-8 and its relay broadcast transmitter was extended by **CRTC **which is valid until 31 August 2018. Ici Radio-Canada Premiere 96.5 FM can listen online with talk, news and current affairs show as well.
